'''Jessica Melbourne-Thomas''' (born 17 May 1981) is an Australian science leader with [[Parks Australia]]. Her research focuses on [[climate change]], its effects on the marine environment, and how to adapt and response to these changes.

== Early life and education ==
Jessica Melbourne-Thomas was born on 17 May 1981.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.women.tas.gov.au/tasmanian_honour_roll_of_women/inductees/2023/dr-jess-melbourne-thomas|title=Dr Jess Melbourne-Thomas|publisher=[[Tasmanian Honour Roll of Women]]|date=2023|access-date=11 September 2023}}</ref>

She completed her undergraduate degree at the [[University of Tasmania]] in 2002. She then moved to the UK to the [[University of Oxford]] to undertake her [[Rhodes Scholarship]] from 2003 to 2005 working on [[coral]] community dynamics.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=http://rhodesproject.com/jess-melbourne-thomas-profile/|title=Jess Melbourne-Thomas Profile|website=The Rhodes Project |access-date=2018-04-15}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scienceandtechnologyaustralia.org.au/profile/dr-jess-melbourne-thomas/|title=Dr Jess Melbourne-Thomas|website=Science & Technology Australia |access-date=2018-07-07}}</ref>

In 2010 she completed her PhD, which developed modelling tools to assist managers in their management of coral reefs, at the [[University of Tasmania]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=http://www.antarctica.gov.au/science/meet-our-scientists/dr-jessica-melbourne-thomas|title=Dr Jessica Melbourne-Thomas|website=Australia Antarctic Division|publisher=Australian Government|access-date=2018-04-15|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180313031746/http://www.antarctica.gov.au/science/meet-our-scientists/dr-jessica-melbourne-thomas|archive-date=13 March 2018}}</ref>

== Career ==
Melbourne-Thomas is the Director of Conservation Science with Parks Australia.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr Jess Melbourne-Thomas {{!}} Centre for Marine Socioecology |url=https://marinesocioecology.org/team/dr-jess-melbourne-thomas/ |access-date=2026-08-24 |website=marinesocioecology.org/ |language=en-AU}}</ref> Her work focuses on bridging the gap between complex scientific research and decision-making for sustainability, particularly in relation to [[climate change adaptation]]. She worked as a [[marine ecologist]] and [[knowledge broker]] with CSIRO and as an ecosystem modeller and science communicator with the Australian Antarctic Division.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://people.csiro.au/m/j/jess-melbourne-thomas|title=Dr Jessica Melbourne-Thomas|website=CSIRO|access-date=2020-01-21}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.canberratimes.com.au/story/6446668/female-scientist-tas-aussie-of-the-year/?cs=14231|title=Female scientist Tas Aussie of the Year|work=Canberra Times|date=18 October 2019|access-date=2020-01-21}}</ref> She was a lead author for the [[Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change|IPCC]]'s Special Report on Oceans and Cryosphere in a Changing Climate in 2019.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.utas.edu.au/news/2017/11/30/479-modelling-marine-futures-with-maths/|title=Modelling marine futures with maths|website=The University of Tasmania |date=30 November 2017 |access-date=2018-04-15}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-501299170.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180715064433/https://www.highbeam.com/doc/1G1-501299170.html|archive-date=15 July 2018|title=Australia: Ecosystems Expert to Compile Collective Climate Change Knowledge|date=21 August 2017|work=Mena Report|access-date=12 July 2018 |url-access=subscription|url-status=usurped|via=HighBeam Research}}</ref>

Melbourne-Thomas is highly engaged in science communication and the translation of science into decision-making, including through outreach to end-users and policy briefings. She is a co-presenter for the [[Massive open online course|Massive Open Online Course]] (MOOC) on Open2Study entitled Marine and Antarctic Science.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.open2study.com/courses/marine-and-antarctic-science|title=Marine and Antarctic Science (Marine)|website=Open 2 Study |access-date=2018-04-15}}</ref> She was named Tasmania's Young Tall Poppy of the Year in 2015 and was one of Science and Technology Australia's first 30 [[Superstars of STEM]].<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|url=http://www.aips.net.au/tall-poppies/tas-tall-poppies/past-tas-tall-poppy-winners/2015-tasmanian-tall-poppy-winners/|title=2015 Tasmanian Tall Poppy Winners|work=AIPS|date=2015|access-date=15 April 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190328171428/http://www.aips.net.au/tall-poppies/tas-tall-poppies/past-tas-tall-poppy-winners/2015-tasmanian-tall-poppy-winners/|archive-date=28 March 2019}}</ref>

Melbourne-Thomas was also the co-founder, along with business entrepreneur Fabian Dattner, of the first [[Homeward Bound (expedition)|Homeward Bound]] voyage, which is an Australian-led, global initiative to foster women's leadership in science.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/entry/largest-ever-all-female-expedition-sets-sail-for-antarctica_us_584191c4e4b017f37fe425e4|title=Largest Ever All-Female Expedition Sets Sail For Antarctica|website=[[HuffPost]] |date=3 December 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.vogue.com.au/gamechangers/technology-and-business/homeward-bound/news-story/095f8341c7ade07228dfd1da00b12bbf|title=Homeward Bound Vogue Game Changers 2018 - Vogue Australia|date=12 March 2018|website=[[Vogue (magazine)|Vogue]]|access-date=2018-07-11}}</ref> Recognizing the difficulties women in science careers have in obtaining funding, balancing the demands of families and careers, the initiative is privately funded.<ref name=BBC2016>{{cite news|title=Largest all-women expedition heads to Antarctica|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/world-australia-38139925|work=[[BBC]]|date=1 December 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170614185020/https://www.bbc.com/news/world-australia-38139925|archive-date=14 June 2017|location=London, England}}</ref> Her role was to coordinate the science program for the 2016 Homeward Bound program.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.cnn.com/2017/06/22/world/homeward-bound-antarctica/index.html|title=How women in science are setting themselves up to save our planet|last=Scott|first=Katy|date=22 June 2017|work=[[CNN]]|access-date=2018-07-11}}</ref> When challenges prevented the group of 76 global women scientists of varying specialities from sailing out of Australia, Melbourne-Thomas worked to reorganize the launch out of [[Ushuaia]], Argentina.<ref name=BBC2016 /><ref name=Burgos2017>{{cite news|last1=Burgos|first1=Alejandra|title=Antártida, mujeres y liderazgo|url=https://elpais.com/elpais/2017/07/19/planeta_futuro/1500482753_085524.html|work=[[El País]]|date=26 July 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180714203108/https://elpais.com/elpais/2017/07/19/planeta_futuro/1500482753_085524.html|archive-date=14 July 2018|location=Madrid, Spain|language=es|trans-title=Antarctica, women and leadership}}</ref> After completion of the research trip, applications were opened for a second voyage and the team was finalized in 2017. They sailed on their second expedition in 2018.<ref name=Burgos2017 />

She was one of 12 noted female scientists to be featured as a constellation on the ceiling of the [[Grand Central Terminal|Grand Central Station]] (New York City) as part of GE's Balance the Equation Initiative.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.ge.com/reports/rewriting-stars-women-scientists-shine-amid-grand-centrals-constellations/|title=Rewriting The Stars: Women Scientists Shine Amid Grand Central's Constellations - GE Reports|date=2017-09-19|work=GE Reports|access-date=2018-04-15 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thecut.com/2017/09/ge-light-show-at-grand-central-honors-female-scientists.html|title=Female Scientists Will Be Honored in a Light Show at Grand Central|last=Syckle|first=Katie Van|work=The Cut|access-date=2018-04-15 }}</ref>

Melbourne-Thomas is the 2020 Tasmanian Australian of the Year.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dr Jess Melbourne-Thomas {{!}} Australian of the Year |url=https://australianoftheyear.org.au/recipients/dr-jess-melbourne-thomas |access-date=2026-08-25 |website=australianoftheyear.org.au |language=en}}</ref>
